note: Art direction for Flower-Souls (MB1), chosen by the owner on 2026-09-27: the style of the Yao (Dao) ritual painting 'Chia Fin', Guangxi, 1920, Ethnological Museum Berlin (public domain; photo CC0 by Daderot, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Chia_Fin_-_Guangxi_province,_China,_1920_-_Ethnological_Museum,_Berlin_-_DSC01315.JPG). Tày Then and Tào priests use the same painted pantheon.
style: A painting for a collectible card game, in exactly the art style of the reference image: a traditional Yao (Dao) and Tày ritual painting from the mountains of northern Vietnam, polychrome on old paper: a warm vermilion and brick-red ground with a slightly worn, aged paper texture, figures drawn flat and frontal with firm black ink outlines, simple round faces with small calm features and white or pale faces, robes in deep green, indigo blue, black and white with small patterned trims, stylised white cloud scrolls and simple flowers, a naive, folk, hand-painted charm, flat colour with no shading or perspective. Palette: vermilion, brick red, black, deep green, indigo, white, touches of ochre and gold. IMPORTANT: use ONLY the style of the reference: do NOT copy its gods, its horsemen, its rows of figures, its three rosettes, its cartouches or any of its writing. Gentle, kind, kid-friendly, never scary, no weapons. One clear main subject, fully in frame. Absolutely no text, letters, Chinese characters, seals, stamps, symbols, logos, borders, card frames or watermarks.

families.Flower-Souls: Background: the flat vermilion-red ground of the reference, with a sky garden of stylised flowers on thin stems, gold and silver blossoms, and white cloud scrolls.

heroFamilies.Flower-Souls: Background: the flat vermilion-red ground of the reference, with a sky garden of stylised flowers on thin stems, gold and silver blossoms, and white cloud scrolls.

subjects.MB1-H01-kitten: A flower-soul: a tiny child, about the size of a flower, whose round face peeks out from the petals of a big blossom that is also its little dress, with leaves for arms; the littlest flower-soul, the cutest of them all: a round-cheeked baby girl with huge dark eyes and a shy, curious smile, peeking out of a small, still-closed silver flower bud that is her dress, standing on tiptoe on a curling leaf in the sky garden to look down at the world. Not a goddess, no crown, no halo. Tender and captivating.
subjects.MB1-H01-bigcat: A flower-soul: a tiny child, about the size of a flower, whose round face peeks out from the petals of a big blossom that is also its little dress, with leaves for arms; the littlest flower-soul, the cutest of them all: a round-cheeked little girl with huge dark eyes, now in full bloom: her silver flower has opened wide around her like a big shining skirt of petals, she laughs with her arms open, and a shower of small silver and gold petals swirls around her in the red sky garden. Joyful and radiant, still a small child. Not a goddess, no crown.
subjects.MB1-D01: Mẻ Bjoóc, Mother Flower, the kind grandmother who keeps the garden of children's souls in the sky: a gentle old woman with a warm, smiling round face and her hair in a simple dark indigo headscarf, in long indigo and deep green robes, seated in the middle of her sky garden, holding a round tray of gold and silver flowers on her lap; around her, rows of tiny flower-souls (small children's faces in gold and silver blossoms) grow on stems and look up at her fondly. Motherly, calm and loving.
subjects.MB1-D02: A flower-soul: a tiny child, about the size of a flower, whose round face peeks out from the petals of a big blossom that is also its little dress, with leaves for arms; a golden flower-soul: a cheerful little boy with round cheeks and a big grin, peeking out of a wide-open golden flower, bouncing on its stem as if eager to be picked and handed down to a family, a few golden petals flying off.
subjects.MB1-D03: a Then singer tending a flower in the sky garden: a kind young woman in a long indigo robe and a small dark headdress, kneeling beside one drooping silver flower that has a sleepy child's face, gently pouring water from a little gourd onto its roots, a long-necked round gourd lute slung on her back; the flower-child is waking up and smiling again. Tender and hopeful.
